title: The Ember of Ashvale Again
premise: Coral Okonkwo, a mercenary bound by oath to the silent god Ashvale, has spent her whole life in the valley where magic dies at the border — until a child named Iri arrives speaking the First Tongue and bearing an ember of the god's stolen fire inside their chest. Hunted by the Cinder Court, who silenced Ashvale to hoard divine power, Coral and Iri flee the only home she has ever known and discover her own bloodline was the lock on the god's prison. To free Ashvale, Coral must choose between the belonging she finally finds among the god's scattered faithful and the identity she built as a weapon-for-hire. In the end she shatters the prison with her own name, the god wakes diminished and mortal, the Cinder Court falls, and Coral — no longer sworn to anyone — chooses to stay with Iri and the rebuilt faithful in a valley where magic can finally enter.
about_author: Zephyrine Dunmore is the pen name of a former archaeologist who spent a decade cataloguing dead languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about oaths, exile, and the families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A routine contract escorting a merchant ends at the valley border, where Coral's god-blessed blade goes dull and her oath-glyphs fade. Establishes the silent god Ashvale and Coral's hollow devotion. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Dead Season
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. During the first snow, a child — Iri — appears at her door, feverish, speaking a language no living kingdom uses. When Iri touches Coral's oath-glyphs, they burn bright for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder cracking open a closed heart.

chapters.title: The Word That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. Iri remembers only fragments: a burning library, a woman saying 'run.' Their speech, translated by Coral's dying grandmother's notes, contains the name Ashvale — spoken aloud, which should be impossible. Emotional beat: fear of being a burden warring with hope of being understood.

chapters.title: Ashes on the Wind
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Riders in grey arrive asking after a child, led by the charming Serane Voss of the Cinder Court. Coral lies for the first time in her oath-keeping life and feels the lie like a splinter. Emotional beat: the first conscious betrayal of her old certainties.

chapters.title: What the Oath Actually Says
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Examining her oath-contract, Coral finds a clause she never noticed: her service ends 'when the god speaks again.' She realizes the Court wants Iri dead because the child IS the god's voice. Emotional beat: dawning horror that her whole life was a cage with pretty bars.

chapters.title: Leaving the Only Home
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. The pair slip past the border at night. Crossing it, Coral collapses as dormant magic floods her, and Iri sees the mercenary cry for the first time. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of a world suddenly, dangerously alive.

chapters.title: The Road of Broken Shrines
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They travel through countryside dotted with desecrated Ashvale shrines, learning the Court's purge was thorough. An old shrine-keeper, Maren, shelters them and reveals Coral's mother was one of the faithful. Emotional beat: grief for a stolen inheritance.

chapters.title: The Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The antagonist chapter: Serane reports to the Court's Nine, revealing they silenced Ashvale not out of malice but terror — the last time the god woke, a continent burned. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the enemy's fear.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. Iri's ember flares during a nightmare, healing Coral's old war wound. The two bond properly at last; Iri confesses they may not be a messenger but the god's remaining heart. Emotional beat: found-family tenderness shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Faithful in Hiding
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach a hidden enclave of Ashvale's surviving faithful, who recognize Coral's bloodline as the prison-lock. They welcome her — and then ask her to sacrifice herself to free the god. Emotional beat: belonging offered with a price tag.

chapters.title: Nineteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. The enclave's historian explains the god's silencing: Ashvale split their power into embers to stop the Court, and Iri is the last one. Coral learns her mother died sealing the prison — with her own daughter's name as the key. Emotional beat: rage at being an unconsenting instrument.

chapters.title: Serane's Offer
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Court captures Coral and offers her truth: free the god and the burning begins again; kill Iri and the world stays safe. They show her a vision of the last conflagration. Emotional beat: the enemy's argument landing like a hammer.

chapters.title: The Cage of Good Reasons
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Imprisoned, Coral interrogates her own life: every oath, every rule, every 'for your own good.' She realizes the Court and her enclave want the same thing — her choice made for her. Emotional beat: the crucible of identity.

chapters.title: Iri Alone
chapters.summary: Iri's POV. Iri escapes with Maren's help but refuses to abandon Coral, walking into the Court's stronghold unarmed. Their ember answers their courage, waking dormant faithful across the land. Emotional beat: a child choosing bravery over safety.

chapters.title: The Name in the Stone
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In her cell, Coral finally speaks her true name — her mother's sealing-word — and the prison responds. She understands: the lock was never her death, but her consent. Emotional beat: revelation that rewrites everything.

chapters.title: Storming the Cinder Court
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with Iri's rescue woven in. The faithful assault the stronghold; Coral fights her way to Iri while Serane, doubting her Nine, hesitates to kill them. Emotional beat: fury and ferocity in service of love, not duty.

chapters.title: The Nine Speak
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Nine reveal their true plan: not containing the god but devouring the ember to become gods themselves. Serane's faith shatters. Emotional beat: the corrupt exposed by their own hunger for power.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Prison Door
chapters.summary: Coral and Iri's alternating POV. At the prison-heart, Coral must consent freely — knowing Ashvale waking could burn the world again. Iri offers to take the risk alone. Coral refuses to let a child carry it. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — power accepted with open eyes.

chapters.title: When the God Wakes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral speaks her consent; the prison breaks. Ashvale rises — diminished, mortal-adjacent, and grieving — and together god, mercenary, and child turn the Nine's stolen fire back on them. Emotional beat: awe and terror braided into triumph.

chapters.title: What Burns and What Remains
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Court falls; Serane, spared by Iri's mercy, is left to reckon with her complicity. Ashvale, no longer a god to be sworn to, asks Coral what she wants now that no one owns her. Emotional beat: the strange freedom after the war ends.

chapters.title: The Valley, Opened
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They return to the valley, where magic now crosses the border freely. Coral releases her oath formally — and finds she still chooses the god, the child, and the people, freely this time. Emotional beat: home redefined as chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Ember of Ashvale
chapters.summary: Iri's POV, epilogue. A year later: Iri learning to be a child, Coral teaching new faithful, Ashvale tending a garden like any mortal. Iri writes the first line of a new library. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — belonging at last.
